system.summary: A reciprocal substitution of 12 pairs (a-h, b-q, c-r, d-s, e-l, f-t, g-z, i-m, k-x, n-o, p-u, w-y), with i/j and u/v merged, plus a nomenclator of three-digit numbers for titles, names and places in alphabetical order, number words at 805-824, punctuation numbers 830-850 and nulls from 851.

prior_solution.where: No earlier decipherment found by the contributor or the project; the AGAD cards call the letters "nierozwiązany" (unsolved).

conditions.human_role: Prabal Gupta transcribed the letters, ran the solver and built the readings (issues #316, #317, repository prabal-rje/branicki-1757). The project checked the files against each other and the key; it has not seen the scans.

solution.what: The contributor transcribed the cipher of letter 446 from the AGAD scans, then 1398-1400 in two passes each (1398 page 2 stays rough), and corrected his first transcriptions against the scans (820/822/823 are 620/622/623, and others).

A count-matching algorithm on French next-letter counts gave a reciprocal alphabet from the ciphertext of 446: 12 pairs, every cipher letter a plain letter, with i/j and u/v merged. The decryption reads as French.

The same key applied unchanged to the cipher of 1398, 1399 and 1400, three other letters of the fonds (catalogue 1579), reads them as French; the matcher run on 1399 and 1400 alone returns the 446 key on 99.4% and 98.9% of tokens.

The number groups were valued from clear text beside them (Palatin de Trok, Princesse douairière), repeated context and the alphabetical order of the table; number words 805-824 fixed by the dates and sums; readings in French and English for all four letters.
Outside checks by the contributor: the five shares of 1399 add up to the 146,000 francs it states, and the lords, deputies and Boeven are in Konopczyński (1909).

Project check: the decryption of 446 follows from the transcription and key on every line; a lexicon test (about 140 French words) covers 0.53 to 0.59 of the letters of the four letters under the key against at most 0.27 for any of 300 shuffled keys. No scan compared (VERIFICATION.md).

Refresh from the contributor's repository at commit f465095, which carries his later corrections: the transcriptions were checked against the scans and Matuszewicz's memoirs, pages 2 to 4 of 1398 were reread and compared with three blind passes (37 signs changed), 1399 and 1400 and the number code were corrected, and every open group was searched in the other letters, Konopczyński and the memoirs.

Project re-check on the refreshed files: the decryption of 446 follows from the transcription and key on all 58 lines; the word-list test covers 0.54 to 0.60 of the letters of the four letters against at most 0.28 for any of 300 shuffled keys (VERIFICATION.md).

validation.notes: The statistical test needs a French letter model (lang/, fr-modern), whose corpus cannot be fetched from this environment (Gutenberg returns 403). A lexicon test against 300 shuffled keys was used instead (VERIFICATION.md, section 3); it is not the project's n-gram validation.

outcome.method_basis: Contributor's claim: the alphabet was found from the ciphertext of letter 446 by a count-matching algorithm, with no key or crib from outside; the project verified that the decryption follows and reads as French across four letters, but did not repeat the search.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Counted from the reading files: cipher words of the four letters, 369 (446) + 584 (1398) + 725 (1399) + 472 (1400) = 2,150, of which 31 are holes (unread code groups, [?...] stretches and [?word] doubtful readings: 7 + 16 + 6 + 2): 2,119 of 2,150 = 98.6%. Pages 2 to 4 of 1398 were reread with the key in view, so its share is not a blind reading.

texts.label: Branicki to Potocki, Białystok, 22 March 1757 (AGAD 1/338/0/1/446)
texts.summary: Branicki tells Potocki that the plan agreed at Warsaw meets obstacles but must not be lost from sight, that the most pressing matter is the abuse an envoy (probably the stolnik of Lithuania) makes of his mission, and proposes a manifesto to be published together with Potocki's house and other patriots, to meet at the end of the next month.

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as French sentences: the cipher paragraph builds coherent, well-formed clauses; the unspaced decryption is normalised in the reading and a few names are guessed (720 Stolnik, 270/273 Czesnik, 575 Palatin).

texts.label: Marcin Matuszewicz (Matusewic), Jaswojnie, 24 July 1757 (AGAD 1/338/0/1/1398)
texts.summary: A field report from the Russian army under Apraxin at the frontier of Prussia: famine and requisitions in Lithuania, deputies of the Prussian towns come to submit, an army of sixty thousand, rumours of poison in the flour.

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as French sentences, all four pages; pages 2 to 4 were reread by the contributor with the key in view and compared with three blind passes, so the reading is coherent but not blind; a few stretches stay doubtful.

texts.label: Report on the Radziwiłł party, 1756 (AGAD 1/338/0/1/1399)
texts.summary: An insider reports on the party of the Lithuanian grand hetman: a congress at Iwie agrees to deposit 146,000 francs at Koydanow to buy the coming dietines and the Tribunal of 1757, five lords' shares are listed (they add up), and the writer proposes a direct correspondence with the French minister.

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as French sentences: long, well-formed sentences with scattered holes; the shares add up to the stated sum.

texts.label: Boeven to a correspondent, Nieśwież, 11 September 1756 (AGAD 1/338/0/1/1400)
texts.summary: A bloody dietine at Brest, with massacred gentlemen and brother against brother; the rival party has spent 200,000 francs in the palatinates and elected its own deputies; the palatine decides not to risk the party's own money; signed Boeven.

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as French sentences: coherent narrative sentences with few holes; the date is in cipher.
